main_text.p: Relinquitur ergo, actionem & passionem non esse actus reipsa diversos, sed unum tantum, licet di-stinguantur ratione seu intellectu. Quæ in contrarium possint objici, non difficile est diluere. Hæc ve-ro ad intelligendum, quid proprie sit motus, in præ-senti sufficient. Porro ad percipiendum cætera quæ de motu explicari adhuc debet, necessum est, de infinito, de loco, & per contrarium de vacuo, de tempore, quædam præmittamus.
main_text.head: DE INFINITO.
Quare nunc agendum de Infinito?
main_text.p: Lib.1. [?]cap.4.1.PRimò: Cum hæc pars philosophiæ consideret motum, magnitudines, tempus, atque de his quæ-ri soleat, finitáne sint an infinita: consentaneum sanè est, de infinito disputationem instituí.
2.Secundò: Quotquot ferè hactenus physici de na-turalibus differuerunt, sermonem admiscuerunt de infinito. Quamobrem tractatio de infinito præte-riri à nobis nullo modo potest.
main_text.head: AN SIT INFINITVM?
main_text.p: Variæ quidem rationes atq; opiniones à veteri-bus sunt relatæ: nos recensebimus primo loco, quæ in partem affirmativam conveniunt: secundo, quæ in partem negativam: inde conclusionem subiciemus.

page.notes: Printed "Lib.1." in the left margin is uncertain (could read "Lib.ʒ."). The word "objici" is printed with a j-like letter between vowels; read as "objici". "na-turalibus": the line-end hyphen is not clearly visible, so the word is written whole. The page number is printed as "6o" (old form of 60). The running head is copied as printed. No printing errors were noticed, and no illegible lines.
